record.one_liner: Cloud communications platform with APIs for SMS, voice, WhatsApp, email, verification and related messaging/voice services.
record.auth_notes: Both are HTTP Basic auth: API key SID + secret (recommended) or Account SID + Auth Token (required by some endpoints). No documented OAuth for third-party apps on the fetched page; Twilio also has short-lived Access Tokens for client SDKs, but I did not verify that from a fetched page.
record.access_notes: Free trial account (expires 30 days after sign-up) gives the same Account SID/Auth Token and API key management. Limits: send only to up to 5 verified numbers, sign-up country only, Twilio templates only; free units 100 SMS, 100 WhatsApp, 3,000 emails, 75 voice minutes. Upgrading to paid removes restrictions. Production use is pay-as-you-go; SMS in the US also requires sender registration (A2P 10DLC), which I did not verify from a fetched page.
record.blocker: Trial is time-limited and restricted. Production needs a paid account, and likely sender/number registration. The official MCP server is a docs-search server only (public beta, read-only, no API calls). The community/alpha twilio-labs MCP (@twilio-alpha/mcp) wraps the public API but is unsupported. OAuth-based API MCP tools are listed as planned.
